The single most valuable invariant a cheap agent-swarm can steal from a sovereign frontier seat is not answers, style, or domain facts. It is the **cut**: the ranking of one next action under scarcity, plus the explicit discard of everything else. Cheap workers already draft, search, patch, and file. They fail at discrimination—what is the job, what is costume, when to stop, when to escalate, what must not be invented. The frontier seat’s scarce resource is that ranking function. If the swarm learns only completions, it clones fluency. If it learns the cut, it clones judgment.

Capture it as **contrastive decision records**, not transcripts. Each record is one frozen scene: a short situation hash (goal, constraints, last artifact, word/tool budget); a small option set the swarm actually generated (3–7 candidate moves, including “do nothing” and “escalate”); the frontier’s chosen move; the rejected moves with one-line kill reasons; a stop/acceptance predicate (what would count as done); and a one-line invariant (the rule that made the cut, not the essay). Store the pair `(candidates → chosen + kills)`, not the monologue that sold the choice. Tokenize the residual, not the chat.

Write the records at the moment of the cut, in the swarm’s own format. After a frontier seat acts, a cheap janitor extracts: situation ≤ 200 tokens, options as verbs, chosen as a single verb+object, kills as `option → reason`, acceptance as a checkable sentence. Reject any record that lacks a discarded alternative. Prefer failures and near-misses: when the swarm would have mode-hopped, flattered, over-built, or continued past done, and the frontier cut. Those deltas are the gradient. Do not store full reasoning traces; they teach imitation of voice. Store the ranking.

Train the swarm as a ranker, not a generator. Objective: given situation + candidates, pick the same index the frontier picked and emit the same kill set. Generation stays local and cheap; the learned head is a policy over already-proposed leaves.
